PlotPoints.label: Plot Points

Use.takeTheHit: Take the hit for an ally
Use.downgrade: Downgrade a 'Mech hit on a person

PlotPoints.GmSpent: The GM spends a Plot Point
PlotPoints.NoCharacters: No player characters. Assign characters to players in User Configuration.

Edge.label: Edge
Edge.hint: Edge spent this session. Click a pip to mark it; you may spend up to EDG points per session.
Edge.NoneLeft: No Edge left this session, or Edge was already spent on this roll.

Used.highest: Edge: opponent rerolled the highest die

Skill.None: No skills yet. Use + to add one from the Skills List.
Skill.Name: Skill
Skill.KeyHint: Links the skill to the book's Skills List so weapons and Tests can find it.
Skill.Subject: Subject

Trait.ModifierHint: Offered as a checkbox in the Test dialog. Leave 0 for story-only traits.

Effect.label: Rules effect
Effect.hint: Applied automatically: Toughness takes 1 off each hit to the Condition Monitor and Glass Jaw adds 1, Pain Resistance ignores the –1 wound modifier, Unlucky turns 6s on your own Edge rerolls into 1s.

Trait.InitiativeHint: Used only with rolled Initiative, e.g. Combat Sense +1.

Mod.accuracyHint: Accuracy: a negative modifier here is reduced by 1.

Armor.label: Armor
Armor.NaturalHint: Hide or scales of a creature: no pips, the damage reduction always applies.

Gear.Hint: Inventory items have no stats; use them as Cues for your Narrations.

Condition.label: Condition Monitor
Condition.Blocked: Crossed off by a low STR/WIL
Condition.KiaHint: EDG + EDG with no modifiers; starts Easy and gets harder each time.
Condition.WoundsHint: Worst row on each track, added together, applies to all rolls.

Test.Title: Test: {name}
Test.AttributesHint: Used only for attribute-only Tests, e.g. RFL + RFL to catch an object.

Attack.Title: Attack: {weapon}
Attack.OutOfRange: The weapon can't reach that range bracket.
Attack.NoTarget: No token targeted: enter the defender's bonus by hand, or target a token (T) and reopen.
Attack.DefenseModifierHint: Cover, darkness, defensive traits: added to the target's roll.

Damage.Title: {name} is hit
Damage.KiaNeeded: Damage past Staggered: make a KIA Test.

Session.Confirm: Start a new session? Every character goes back to 3 Plot Points and regains all Edge; the GM pool resets to 1.
Session.Started: New session: Plot Points and Edge refreshed.

initiativeMode.name: Turn order
initiativeMode.hint: Narrative: the GM's side first, then players in the order users are listed. Rolled: 2D6 + Initiative bonus (Experience Level and traits), ties by EDG then RFL. Cinematic: the GM sets the order by hand in the tracker.

showPlotPoints.name: Show Plot Points panel on start
showPlotPoints.hint: You can always open it with Shift+P or the star button in the token controls.

MWD.NoActiveGM: No GM is connected to carry this out.

Con.Title: Consciousness Check
Con.Label: CON {n}
Con.Hint: Consciousness Check: raw 2D6 against the CON of the deepest filled Physical row, no modifiers. The book calls for it after damage in 'Mech-Scale Combat (p. 47).
Con.NotNeeded: No full Physical row yet: no CON Check needed.
Con.Unconscious: Unconscious: skips the next Narration, then checks again
Con.FoughtThrough: Fought through it: Plot Point spent, WIL added

Hardware.label: Hardware
Hardware.Hint: Machines this character owns. Board one to pilot it; the character leaves any other machine. You can also drag a 'Mech onto this sheet, or a character onto a 'Mech sheet.

Mech.HeatDissipationHint: Heat tokens shed at the end of each Narration (p. 47)
Mech.DiagramHint: Top row: Armor, bottom row: Structure. Numbers in brackets are 2D6 hit location results. Click a pip to mark damage; the fields set the maximum.

Pilot.label: MechWarrior
Pilot.None: No pilot. Pick one above or drag a character onto this sheet.

Weapon.PrimaryHint: A player character's Primary Weapon deals full damage on a head hit without a Plot Point (p. 45).
Weapon.HeatAlternative: Can deal Heat instead of damage (flamer, "or H")
Weapon.CountHint: Used for indirect hits on people (p. 66).

Equipment.label: Equipment
Equipment.LocationHint: Ammo in a location can explode on a critical hit there (p. 45).

Attack.NoTarget: No 'Mech targeted: enter the defender's bonus by hand, or target a token (T) and reopen.
Attack.JumpTargetHint: You jumped: +1 against the target you picked, –1 against any other (p. 40).
Attack.AutoHint: Added automatically: range, speed (your Max Movement minus the target's), target jumped (–1), shut-down or unconscious target (+2), wounds, Disengaged target (needs 11+).

Physical.Title: Physical attack: {name}
Physical.Hint: Pointblank only. Punch: no arm weapons fired this Narration. Death from Above: needs a jump.
Physical.MovementHint: Charge and Death from Above deal (tonnage / 30) × Movement.

Note.kick: The target must make a Piloting Test to stay standing.
Note.push: The target must make a Piloting Test to stay standing.
Note.charge: Both 'Mechs must make a Piloting Test to stay standing.
Note.dfa: Both 'Mechs must make a Piloting Test to stay standing.
Note.ram: The rammer takes the target's Tonnage/30 in 2-point clusters.

Damage.Glancing: Glancing blow: 1 damage to the head. A Plot Point buys the rest.
Damage.MechDestroyed: The 'Mech is out of the fight.

Crit.label: Critical Hits
Crit.None: Critical hit {location} ({roll}), but nothing left to hit
Crit.GyroDestroyed: gyro destroyed: no Movement, the 'Mech falls
Crit.Engine: engine shielding damaged (+1 Heat each Narration)

Heat.label: Heat
Heat.CarriedHint: Penalties this Narration come from the {n} tokens left after the last cool down.
Heat.AmmoExploded: Ammo explodes ({roll}): the pilot takes 3 damage
Heat.TooHotToRestart: Too hot to restart (more than 3 Heat tokens)

EndNarration.Title: {name}: end of Narration
EndNarration.Hint: CON Check if the pilot is unconscious, cool down, shutdown and ammo checks, engine restart (p. 38, 47–48).

Fall.Title: Fall
Fall.PilotTest: Piloting Test to avoid pilot damage

Vehicle.HasTurretHint: Without a turret there is no Turret location: hit rolls 10–12 go to the Front.
Vehicle.MovementLostHint: Motive damage (–2) and critical hits (–1 or –2).
Vehicle.DiagramHint: Top row: Armor, bottom row: Structure. Any location losing all of its pips destroys the vehicle; nothing transfers. Without a turret, 10–12 hit the front.

Damage.HeatCrits: {n} Heat: one critical hit check per token (vehicles have no Heat scale)
Damage.Immobile: The vehicle is immobile until repaired.

Crit.Crew: crew compartment hit: 3 Physical damage to everyone aboard.
Crit.Stunned: crew stunned: –2 to all Tests during their next Narration.
Crit.Ammo: ammo explosion, the vehicle is destroyed.
Crit.StunRecovered: The crew shakes off the stun.

Vehicle.NoUpkeep: Combat vehicles ignore Heat; nothing to do.

Crash.Title: {name} crashes
Crash.Hint: Treated as a ram: (Tonnage/30) × Movement to the unit in 2-point clusters, and 3 Physical damage per Movement (min. 1) to everyone aboard (p. 49).

Fighter.DiagramHint: Each location has its own Armor; damage past it goes to the shared Structure. 2+ damage to a location from one attack calls for a critical hit check.

Crit.Avionics: avionics damaged: –2 to Piloting Tests; make a Piloting Test.
Crit.FuelExploded: fuel tank hit and explodes ({roll}), the fighter is destroyed.
Crit.FuelHeld: fuel tank hit, but it holds ({roll}).
Crit.Engine: engine shielding damaged: –1 maximum Movement, +2 Heat at the end of the next Narration.
Crit.Ammo: ammo explosion, the fighter is destroyed.
Crit.Cockpit: cockpit hit: the pilot takes 3 Physical damage.

Damage.PilotingTest: Piloting Test to stay in control.

Fighter.OutOfControl: {name} is out of control: no Movement or attacks until a Piloting Test at the end of a later Narration succeeds.

Warn.OutOfControl: The fighter is out of control.
Warn.NoPhysical: Aerospace fighters cannot make physical attacks.

Mixed.RollHitType: Roll for direct or indirect hit
Mixed.KilledBy: Killed in Action by a direct hit: {source}.
Mixed.SmallArmsNoDamage: Not enough to hurt it yet.

alternateId.name: Alternate ID
alternateId.hint: You lead a double life; you or the GM can bring it into the story.

attractive.name: Attractive
attractive.hint: +1 to CHA Tests where looks matter.

citizenship.name: Citizenship
citizenship.hint: +1 to CHA Tests with citizens of your faction.

combatSense.name: Combat Sense
combatSense.hint: Pick your place in the turn order without a Plot Point.

connections.name: Connections
connections.hint: +1 to CHA Tests with your connections.

equipped.name: Equipped
equipped.hint: At creation: 1 extra weapon or 2 extra Inventory items. Not for XP.

gTolerance.name: G-Tolerance
gTolerance.hint: Ignore modifiers for high-g maneuvers and zero gravity.

goodReputation.name: Good Reputation
goodReputation.hint: +1 to CHA Tests with people who know you.

painResistance.name: Pain Resistance
painResistance.hint: Ignore the first wound modifier on both tracks.

prosthetic.name: Prosthetic
prosthetic.hint: Cancels Lost Limb while worn; needs Lost Limb.

rank.name: Rank
rank.hint: Needed for Captain or higher; you command a unit.

sixthSense.name: Sixth Sense
sixthSense.hint: +1 to Perception Tests against surprise and ambush.

thickSkinned.name: Thick-Skinned
thickSkinned.hint: Ignore modifiers for extreme heat and cold.

toughness.name: Toughness
toughness.hint: 1 less Physical and Fatigue damage from each hit.

wealthy.name: Wealthy
wealthy.hint: +1 Hardware Point at creation. Not for XP.

badReputation.name: Bad Reputation
badReputation.hint: –1 to CHA Tests with people who know you.

bloodmark.name: Bloodmark
bloodmark.hint: There is a price on your head; the GM can use it.

combatParalysis.name: Combat Paralysis
combatParalysis.hint: Always take the last Narration in a round.

compulsion.name: Compulsion
compulsion.hint: –1 to Tests to resist your compulsion.

darkSecret.name: Dark Secret
darkSecret.hint: –1 to Tests to keep your secret.

dependents.name: Dependents
dependents.hint: Someone depends on you; the GM can use it.

enemy.name: Enemy
enemy.hint: A nemesis can turn up at any time.

glassJaw.name: Glass Jaw
glassJaw.hint: 1 more Physical and Fatigue damage from each hit.

inForLife.name: In for Life
inForLife.hint: You belong to a shadowy organization; the GM can use it.

lostLimb.name: Lost Limb
lostLimb.hint: –4 to Tests using the missing limb.

poor.name: Poor
poor.hint: At creation: 1 weapon, 2 Inventory items, half the Hardware Points (at least 1).

thinSkinned.name: Thin-Skinned
thinSkinned.hint: Double modifiers for extreme heat and cold.

tds.name: TDS (Transit Disorientation Syndrome)
tds.hint: –2 to all Tests for 20 minutes after a hyperspace jump.

unattractive.name: Unattractive
unattractive.hint: –1 to CHA Tests where looks matter.

unlucky.name: Unlucky
unlucky.hint: 6s on your own Edge rerolls count as 1s.

Creation.Title: Character creation: {name}
Creation.FinishWithIssues: {n} rule problems are left. The GM may allow them. Finish anyway?
Creation.ReplaceItems: The character's {n} skills, traits, weapons, armor and Inventory items will be replaced by the ones from the wizard. Continue?
Creation.AnySkill: +1 to any Skill except Artillery, Gunnery, Piloting, Support Weapons

Hint.theme: A few words on who the character is, a name and some one-word Tags (p. 68).
Hint.faction: The nation or group the character is loyal to (p. 69).
Hint.experience: Sets the points for Attributes and Skills, the number of weapons and Hardware Points (p. 69).
Hint.attributes: Every Attribute starts at 1 and goes up to 4 here. Each point of EDG above 1 costs 2 (p. 70).
Hint.skills: Each Skill takes at least 1 point and at most 4. Take at least one Knowledge Skill (p. 70).
Hint.traits: One or two positive Traits and as many negative ones (p. 72).
Hint.lifeModules: One module for Childhood, Higher Education (optional) and Real Life; each gives +1 to a Skill, or the Skill at 1 (p. 73).
Hint.weapons: Weapons by experience level, plus Unarmed or Martial Arts for free (p. 75).
Hint.inventory: Up to four non-combat items without stats (p. 75).
Hint.hardware: One starting unit within your Hardware Points; leftover points turn into XP, Skill points or EDG (p. 76).
Hint.cues: Catchphrases and bold lines the character might say, one per line (p. 77).
Hint.background: Personal data, history, personality and Dispositions (p. 77).

Creation.ThemePlaceholder: e.g. grizzled tank sergeant with an attitude
Creation.FactionModule: The faction is also the character's Faction Life Module.
Creation.LevelBudget: {attributes} Attribute points, {skills} Skill points, {weapons} weapons, {hardware} Hardware Points
Creation.LevelGroupRule: At least half the group plays the chosen level, and nobody is more than two levels away from it (p. 69).
Creation.ConditionHint: STR and WIL below 5 cross off pips on the Condition Monitor; the sheet does that by itself.
Creation.SkillsRules: Gunnery and Piloting are taken separately for BattleMechs, combat vehicles and aerospace fighters.
Creation.TraitsRules: Your own Traits give at most +1 or –1 to any one thing.
Creation.LifeModulesRules: Greyed-out modules need another module first, e.g. Tour of Duty needs a military education.
Creation.EquippedHint: Equipped: one more weapon, or two more Inventory items.
Creation.WeaponsRules: Pick from the list, drag a weapon here from the sidebar or a compendium, or invent one from a comparable weapon's stats. At most {max} weapons in total. Invented weapons cannot be customized later.
Creation.InventoryRules: Inventory items are Cues with no rules; skip ammo and other mundane things.
Creation.NoUnits: No units you can use yet. The GM creates the 'Mech, vehicle or fighter and gives you ownership.
Creation.DispossessedHint: All Hardware Points are kept for later; the first 'Mech bought with them costs 1 less (p. 76).
Creation.HardwarePool: Hardware Pool: the group pooled its points
Creation.HardwarePoolHint: With the group's agreement, a unit may cost more than your own Hardware Points (p. 76).

Issue.skillSpecialty: {skill}: choose BattleMech, combat vehicle or aerospace fighter.
Issue.knowledgeNeeded: Take at least one Knowledge Skill.
Issue.traitsNeeded: Take at least one positive and one negative Trait.
Issue.traitsMax: At most {max} Traits of each kind.
Issue.traitsBalance: Positive and negative Traits must match ({positive} and {negative}).
Issue.traitModifier: {name}: your own Traits give at most ±1.
Issue.lifeModuleSpecialty: {slot}: choose the hardware for Gunnery or Piloting.
Issue.weaponsTotal: No more than {max} weapons in total, counting the free melee option.
Issue.hardwareOver: The unit costs {cost} Hardware Points, you have {budget}.
Issue.hardwareSkills: A {type} needs the right Gunnery and Piloting.
Issue.conversion: {unspent} unspent Hardware Points, {converted} converted: convert them all.

Advance.label: Character Advancement
Advance.Hint: Spend XP between Missions (p. 77–78). The latest purchase can be undone from the log.
Advance.NeedSpecialty: Choose the hardware for Gunnery or Piloting.
Advance.NeedSubject: A Knowledge Skill needs a subject.
Advance.HasSkill: The character already has this Skill.
Advance.BuyTraitHint: {cost} XP, with a Narration of how the character gained it. Equipped and Wealthy cannot be bought.
Advance.RemoveTraitConfirm: Remove {name} for {cost} XP? Tell the story of how the character overcame it.
Advance.WeaponsHint: {cost} XP each, once per weapon: Accuracy cancels one –1 modifier, Lethality adds 1 damage, Range improves one range bracket by 1.
Advance.CannotCustomize: This weapon cannot take that customization.
Advance.RangeHint: The penalty in that bracket goes down by 1.
Advance.AcquireHint: Salvage needs a unit defeated in the last Mission; repairing or rebuilding it is paid separately.
Advance.HowBuy: Buy: its Hardware Points in XP (+{mech} for a 'Mech)
Advance.HowSalvage: Salvage: its Hardware Points –{n} in XP
Advance.NoUnits: No units you own to acquire. The GM creates the unit and gives you ownership.
Advance.NotUnitOwner: You do not own that unit.
Advance.AwardHint: Mission objectives, plus 1 for a clever or bold Narration (p. 77).
Advance.AwardGmOnly: Only the GM can take back awarded XP.
Advance.UndoRepairHint: The XP comes back, but the unit stays repaired.

Crew.label: Built-in crew
Crew.Hint: For NPC units: the crew lives in the unit itself, so every token has its own. It flies or drives whenever nobody is in the pilot's seat.
Crew.Standby: Stands by while the pilot is aboard.
Crew.LevelHint: Choosing a level fills in Gunnery, Piloting and Initiative; you can change them afterwards.
Crew.StrHint: Sets the Physical track of the crew's Condition Monitor.
Crew.WilHint: Sets the Fatigue track of the crew's Condition Monitor.
